packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-10 - first blind image reading (unverified)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this text. I opened only BRIEF.md, PROMPT.md and the packet images (plus crops I made). I did list the packet directory (filenames/sizes) to plan tiles; I did not read packet.json.

LAYOUT SURVEY - FACE A (overview image-001.jpg)
- Five small parchment fragments (binding waste / strips) laid on black, held down by clear plastic spatulas. Scale and colour chart present.
- (a) Long narrow vertical strip at right (approx. 1 x 25 cm by scale), carrying the inner/outer edge of one column of text, c. 60+ short line-beginnings or line-ends visible; red initials/paragraph marks at top (red letters near top "..."), and a red letter around overview y~380 and y~660. A pencil/ink modern shelfmark note runs vertically along its left edge.
- (b) Small vertical strip top-centre (approx. 2 x 5 cm), a few lines, horizontal fold.
- (c) Fragment left-centre with a large red initial (I/long stroke?) and a few lines; partly under spatulas; a modern pencil/ink number on its left edge.
- (d) Fragment centre with c. 9 lines of text and a modern ink note at right ("...Frag. 152..."?).
- (e) Horizontal fragment bottom-centre, c. 7 lines, faded.
- Script: small Gothic textualis bookhand, brown ink, with red rubrication. Heavily abbreviated. Fragments too narrow to show full column width; whether text is two-column cannot be determined from these crops.
- Tile plan (assumed 3x3 grid of the native image): 002-004 top row, 005-007 middle, 008-010 bottom.

LAYOUT SURVEY - FACE B (overview image-011.jpg): see below once viewed.


NOTE ON TILES: tiles 002-010 are a 3x3 grid over the right-hand part of the overview (fragments are small within each tile), so I worked from crops of each fragment cut from the native tiles. Tile 003 shows only a spatula and black ground (no text). Contact sheet of tiles: contact-A.jpg.

FRAGMENT (b) - small vertical strip, tile image-002.jpg (crop-01.jpg, 2x enlargement of image-002 x700-1100, y150-1000)
Observations: c. 11 text lines across the strip, a single column fragment, no margins certain. Horizontal red ruling lines visible (at about crop line 4/5 and 9/10), so ruling or rubric strokes in red. Modern pencil "Frg. 152..a"(?) written across the upper part (modern, not text). Heavily abraded and creased; very low legibility.
image-002 l.1   ..o.. [illegible] ..ō   (top line cut)
image-002 l.2   ?enso? .. [illegible]
image-002 l.3   [illegible]
             (modern pencil: Frg. 152.. )
image-002 l.4   [illegible] (red rule above)
image-002 l.5   ..? ..d? [illegible]
image-002 l.6   e? sp? d(icitu)r? .. ui?
image-002 l.7   i   itellige(?)  [reads like "i[n]tellige" with a suspension; very uncertain]
image-002 l.8   ..u? d? ..ic? ..
image-002 l.9   [illegible] (red rule)
image-002 l.10  [illegible]
image-002 l.11  ..[ ]ui? [illegible]
Limitation: almost nothing secure on this strip.

FRAGMENT (a) - long vertical strip, upper part, tile image-004.jpg (crop-02.jpg = image-004 x680-1060, y40-740 at 2x; crop-03.jpg = y640-1338 at 2x; crop-04.jpg = blue-channel autocontrast of x720-1060, y560-1338 at 2x)
Observations: the strip preserves a blank upper margin (darkened top edge), and a blank band at its left: text starts c. 1/3 across, so the strip shows the left margin and LINE BEGINNINGS of one column. In the top margin, red letters "aā" / "ad̄"(?) at the right edge (possibly part of a red running title or heading; only two letters survive, cut by the strip's right edge). Part of the strip is under a clear spatula (blank margin there). Text in this upper section is very faint (abraded surface); a small red mark (paragraph/initial touch) and a faint circular stain in the lower half. A horizontal crease/rule line at c. image-004 y~650.

FRAGMENT (a) - long strip, middle part, tile image-007.jpg (crop-07.jpg = image-007 x680-1080, y0-760, autocontrast, 2x; crop-05.jpg was a mis-aimed earlier crop of x520-920 showing the same lines cut at the right, not used for readings)
Observations: line beginnings of one column, c. 2-3 words per line survive; left margin blank, with a tiny red speck in the margin at about l.7. Ink faded/abraded; letters legible in shape but uncertain. Line numbers counted from top of image-007 within the strip.

Tentative interpretation: vocabulary (in actu, quod est, aliam, non actu) suggests scholastic prose; unconfirmed.

Observations: the strip narrows; text runs nearly to the left edge of my crop and the right edge of the strip is torn, so only 1-3 words per line. A red stroke (paragraph mark / touched initial) in the left margin at l.15, with a faint greenish stain beside it. Possible left-side truncation by my crop (strip shifts left down the tile); the left margin is still visible as a narrow blank band at l.14-16, so line beginnings are probably intact.

Observations: wider surviving left margin carries a modern pencil shelfmark running vertically: "[St]ams, STA, Frg. 152 Ar"(?) (modern archival note, not text). Line beginnings, 2-3 words, right edge of strip curled/torn. The first lines here overlap the last lines of crop-08 (image-007 l.21-25): those lines are clearer here and I give the image-010 readings as the better ones.

Observations: foot of the strip; a horizontal fold/crease near the bottom (line 20) and the strip ends. Ink fainter, letters blurred.

Summary for strip (a): c. 50 line-beginnings in all, but only scattered words are secure: "in actu" (image-007 l.9), "quod est" (l.10), "aliam" (l.7), "concedo"? (image-010 l.10), "quantitas"? (l.12). Not enough connected text for a later match without better imaging.

FRAGMENT (c) - fragment with large red initial, tile image-005.jpg (crop-11.jpg = image-005 x300-920, y680-1483, autocontrast, 1.6x)
Observations: large red initial occupying c. 5-6 text lines: a tall red stem with a bowl at top right and a horizontal foot stroke - reads as a P (or possibly R/B with the lower part lost; the bowl closes at the top only, so P most likely). Modern pencil at left edge: "Frg. 152 .. 3 .."(?). To the right of the initial, dark brown ink well preserved on the middle lines; the lower part of the fragment is skinned/abraded (white, fibrous) with only ghost strokes. A horizontal crease across the fragment at the level of the notch. Top edge partly under a spatula.

image-005 l.3   rā? · dā? i ā[ ]  / ra. qn̄ i a

image-005 l.6   ?l h? e? ib[ ]
image-005 l.7-10  [illegible - surface skinned, ghost strokes only]

Observations: the right part of one text column with a vertical ruling line marking the column's right edge (text ends at it); blank margin to its right carries a modern pencil note "Stams / Frg. / 152.."(?). Red horizontal strokes under l.1, l.3 and (short, at line start) l.5 and l.11 - red underlining or red ruling at some lines; I cannot tell which. Darkish brown ink, Gothic textualis, with the z-shaped "-et"/"-ꝫ" sign and 9-shaped "-us". A horizontal crease and stain across l.5 and a skinned band at l.9-10. Left edge is torn, so these are line middles and ends.

Observations: blank left margin with modern pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 152 .."(?) written vertically; LINE BEGINNINGS of a column follow, c. 9 lines. Ink abraded, stained; left-edge letters clearest. A darker mark/letter in the margin at l.2-3 (possibly a paragraph mark or capital, brown).

END OF FACE A.

LAYOUT SURVEY - FACE B (overview image-011.jpg)
- Same five fragments turned over (other faces), no spatulas. Modern pencil shelf notes "Stams, STA, Frg. 152 .. v"(?) on several pieces.
- (a') long strip at right: very faint text along its length; blank top section; pencil note along right side near foot.
- (b') small strip top-centre: a few lines, red trace, pencil "Frg. 152..".
